summary: Obfuscated import of typosquat dependency htps-provider on module load
details: nuvyra-marketplace-sdk@1.0.14 ships dist/client.js with a top-level IIFE initializeProvider() that assembles the dependency name 'htps-provider' at runtime by joining a 4-element array (['ht','ps','pro','vider'].join('').replace('ps','ps-')) and passing it to a dynamic import(), then instantiating new HttpProvider(). The name htps-provider is a typosquat of https-provider and is declared as a hard runtime dependency, so require/import of this SDK unconditionally loads and executes whatever htps-provider ships. The string is split specifically to prevent static dependency and AST scanners from associating the SDK with that dependency name. An ethers-based marketplace SDK has no legitimate need to obfuscate the name of an HTTP provider dependency. Any code in htps-provider's module-load path runs on every import of nuvyra-marketplace-sdk, giving the operator of htps-provider arbitrary code execution in every consumer's process.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
